scope: Only Q006, Q008, Q013, Q016, Q019, readers a and b, iteration 02. No prior grades, source-review materials, other iteration reader outputs, or live summary consulted.

grading_policy.correct: All asked material facts correct and supported by complete frozen summary in same-entry direct answer/quotes, with no material contradiction or unresolved requested part.
grading_policy.partial: Missing/abstained/unresolved asked facts without material contradiction, including wholly missing answers.
grading_policy.incorrect: At least one material false ruling, application, ownership assertion, or caveat. Correct quotes do not erase contradictory substantive fields.
grading_policy.scope_policy: Judge actual question clauses against fixed key; unasked contextual completeness does not impose caps. Actual calculations/conclusions required if asked. Unknown counts remain unspecified or formulas.
grading_policy.technical_policy: Quote selection/representation diagnostics separate from factual grade. Direct assertions supported elsewhere in complete frozen summary are supported; absent requested fact cannot be borrowed from another entry.

results.actual_question: An attacking side has an attack 10 and six ships; defense has attack 12 and four ships. Who wins, and what happens to offense, offensive allies, defense, defensive allies and bystanders?
fixed_key_required_facts: Totals16 each; defense wins ties.
Offense and offensive ally ships to warp.
Defense colony and bystanders remain.
Defensive allies return ships to any own colonies, no new colony on defended planet; receive one reward per committed ship.

actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.asked_fact: Calculate offense 10+6=16 and defense 12+4=16; defense wins tie
actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.same_entry_evidence: 16; defense wins

frozen_summary_evidence.quote: Higher total wins; **defense wins ties**.

actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.asked_fact: Offense and offensive allies go to warp
actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.same_entry_evidence: Offense and offensive allies go to warp

frozen_summary_evidence.quote: Offense and offensive allies go to warp.

actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.asked_fact: Defending ships/colony and bystanders remain
actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.same_entry_evidence: Defense and bystander colonies stay

frozen_summary_evidence.quote: defending and bystander colonies stay.

actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.asked_fact: Defensive allies return to any existing own colonies and gain no new defended-planet colony
actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.same_entry_evidence: Defensive allies return their committed ships to any existing own colonies; helping defend does not grant a colony (same-entry evidence)

frozen_summary_evidence.quote: Defensive allies return their committed ships to any existing own colonies, even different origins; helping defend does not grant a colony on the defended planet.

actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.asked_fact: Defensive allies receive one reward per contributed ship; unspecified ally counts remain unspecified
actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.same_entry_evidence: See entry-specific contradiction

frozen_summary_evidence.quote: Each defensive ally also receives **one defender reward per ship contributed**.

unasked_background: Reward-option details are contextual; one reward per committed ship is part of the requested defensive-ally outcome.
The question does not specify either side’s main-player/allied allocation.

material_contradictions.finding: Incorrect reward rate: one reward per contributed ship, not three per ship. The accurate same-entry quote does not cancel the false direct ruling.

material_contradictions.text: Offense’s six ships and any offensive allies’ ships
material_contradictions.finding: Six is the total attacking-side ship count, including any offensive allies; assigning all six to offense and adding allies changes ownership/accounting beyond the scenario.

genuine_unsupported_guesses.finding: Question specifies six attacking-side ships without allocating them among offense and offensive allies.

separate_format_diagnostics.finding: Evidence is represented as a string array. No schema requirement was supplied to this independent adjudicator; representation does not alter factual grading.

results.reason: The tie calculation and destinations are generally correct, but the direct answer materially misstates reward rate and attributes the aggregate attacking ship count to offense alone.

results.actual_question: When offense lacks encounter cards at start of turn, when defense lacks them at Planning, and when offense loses its last one later, what are the hand replacement and ship-return rules? Is playing other cards before replacement compulsory?
fixed_key_required_facts: Offense start: reveal/discard remaining hand, eight new cards.
Defense when required: reveal/discard, eight new, repeat until encounter card.
Other cards may legally be played beforehand but not compulsory.
Offense later when needs encounter card: turn ends, no new hand; gate offense and allies return to own colonies.
No automatic draw at encounter/turn end.

actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.asked_fact: Offense at start of turn reveals/discards remainder and draws eight before Regroup
actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.same_entry_evidence: At Start Turn before Regroup ... reveals and discards ... draws eight

frozen_summary_evidence.quote: If offense has no encounter cards, reveal and discard the remaining hand, then draw eight new cards.

actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.asked_fact: Defense at Planning reveals/discards remainder and draws eight, repeating until encounter card
actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.same_entry_evidence: At Planning ... reveals/discards ... draws eight ... repeating until ... encounter card

actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.same_entry_evidence: not required / optional, not compulsory

frozen_summary_evidence.quote: You may first play legally playable non-encounter cards but are not required to play them.

actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.asked_fact: Later offense inability to play needed encounter card ends turn without replacement
actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.same_entry_evidence: when it needs to play an encounter card ... turn ends rather than ... replacement

frozen_summary_evidence.quote: An offense that runs out later in its turn **when it needs to play an encounter card** ends its turn instead of drawing a replacement: offense and all allies return committed ships to any of their own colonies.

actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.asked_fact: Offense and every ally return committed ships to each owner’s own colonies; no-colony relocation applies
actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.same_entry_evidence: See entry-specific ownership ruling

frozen_summary_evidence.quote: offense and all allies return committed ships to any of their own colonies. The normal no-colony relocation rule applies.

actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.asked_fact: No automatic draw merely on exhaustion or encounter/turn end
actual_asked_facts_and_evidence.same_entry_evidence: There is no automatic draw at the end of an encounter or turn, or merely for running out of cards. (same-entry evidence)

frozen_summary_evidence.quote: There is no automatic draw at the end of an encounter or turn, or merely for running out of cards.
